A safety fix for S7 writes and the S7 connection. Everybody who writes to a PLC with
`s7 write` should upgrade.

## Highlights

- **A write is not sent again after a lost answer.** Before, when the PLC did a write but its
  answer did not come (timeout, lost connection), the node reconnected, sent the same write a
  second time and reported success. The second write could overwrite a value that the PLC had
  changed in the meantime, for example a command bit that the PLC had already reset. Now the
  write fails with an error that starts with `not confirmed`. Read the tag to see the value in
  the PLC. A write that fails before it reaches the PLC (a dead connection) is still retried.
  The same rule applies to the `setClock` action and the clock set of `syncClock` (`s7 info`),
  and to S7CommPlus writes and alarm acknowledgement.
- **An answer to another request is refused.** Before, an answer with another S7 PDU reference
  than the request was taken as the answer, so a read could show values that did not belong to
  it. Now the client reconnects and asks again.
- **No connection attempts after a flow is removed.** Before, after a deploy that removed or
  changed an endpoint, the old connection could still make its remaining connection attempts.
  Now they stop at once.

Thanks to [Missel2/s7-compatibility-lab](https://github.com/Missel2/s7-compatibility-lab),
whose independent tests found these three cases. Their tests pass with this release.

## Upgrade notes

- A write whose answer is lost now raises an error (`not confirmed …`) instead of a retry that
  often reported success. Flows that must know the result can catch the error (Catch node) and
  read the tag.
